Definition: to breathe; passively, to be breathed upon, i.e. (figuratively) refreshed (as if by a current of air)
BiblicalUsage: Naphesh as a verb means to breathe again or be refreshed, to take a breath after weariness, and it is the Sabbath word. In 2 Samuel 16:14 the king and all the people with him come weary and refresh themselves, and in Exodus 23:12 the seventh day is for rest, so that the ox and the ass may rest and the stranger may be refreshed.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that refreshment is God's idea, not man's luxury, because He built it into the week; the weary king and the stranger at the gate both get the same rest, and the rest is holy.
